correctness.rationale: Affine normalization reduces the theorem to an exact nine-point calculation for the bilinear polynomial \(P(X,Y)=a+bX+cY+dXY\). Rowwise linearity gives at most one zero per nonzero row; a full zero row forces the factorization \(P(X,Y)=(X-\alpha)(b+dY)\), hence exactly three or five zeros. Five explicit nonzero coefficient vectors realize all allowed counts. Exact arithmetic in the packaged verifier corroborates the local rank patterns.

value.rationale: The affine parallelogram is the canonical rank-two product support in \(\mathbb F_3^d\). Its complete spectrum is a natural structural invariant, and the forbidden intermediate size is not visible from a minimum-support uncertainty bound. The theorem is uniform in ambient dimension, exact, and proved by a reusable factorization mechanism rather than by a finite census.
